items.text: Leaving Southampton the liner New York broke her moorings in our wash and nearly struck us; the tug Vulcan pulled her clear
The coal strike is over, but the line took coal from the other ships to fill our bunkers, and half the passengers were moved over from them
She is the largest ship afloat and this is her maiden voyage
Colonel and Mrs Astor came aboard at Cherbourg, back from their winter in Egypt; she is very young and expecting, they say
The Captain is to retire after this crossing; it is his last command before he goes ashore for good
They say we will light the last boilers and try for New York on Tuesday night, a day early
More boilers were lit today and she is making better speed than yesterday
The day's run was posted at noon by the smoking room: a fine figure, and the pool on it was won by a gentleman from Philadelphia
There has been a fire smouldering in one of the coal bunkers since before we sailed; the stokers have been raking it out
The lookouts have no glasses in the crow's nest: the key to the locker went ashore with an officer who left the ship at Southampton
A fireman slipped ashore at Queenstown by hiding in the mail bags on the tender
Somebody saw a stoker's black face peering out of the after funnel at Queenstown; the old hands call it a bad sign
The bumboat women from Queenstown came aboard selling Irish lace; one lady in the first class paid a fortune for a shawl
There was to have been a boat drill this morning, but the Captain cancelled it and held the service instead
The temperature has fallen sharply since dinner; the deck is bitterly cold and the sea is like glass
The carpenter has been told to watch the fresh water: it may freeze tonight, it is so cold
Caronia reports bergs, growlers and field ice in 42 N from 49 to 51 W
Baltic reports icebergs and large quantities of field ice in 41 51 N, 49 52 W; the Captain showed it to the chairman of the line
Californian reports three large bergs five miles to the southward of her, in 42 3 N, 49 9 W
The Second Officer told the crow's nest to keep a sharp lookout for small ice and growlers until daylight
The wireless set broke down on Friday night and the operators worked for hours to mend it; now they are buried in passengers' messages for Cape Race
There are card sharps travelling in the smoking room under false names; a gentleman was warned off a game last night
